guide.metaDescription: Learn how to create, package, publish, and import power-tv theme packages.
guide.heroTitleLine2: to a new living room style.
guide.heroDescription: power-tv theme packages contain only configuration and images, never executable code. Start from the official template, finish your palette, and publish it to the community.
guide.formatsDescription: All three formats use the same theme.json. They differ only in whether image assets are included.
guide.pthemeDescription: Recommended. It is a ZIP container that can carry a preview image and backdrop, making it easy to share between power-tv and the community.
guide.zipDescription: Identical to .ptheme content, only the extension differs. Works well with common archive tools for building and inspection.
guide.jsonDescription: Upload theme.json directly for color-only themes. It cannot reference a backdrop image and does not include a separate preview.
guide.stepsDescription: Start with a minimal working version, then add the dark scheme and assets.
guide.step1Description: Copy the official template and start editing. It includes the required fields; the JSON Schema enables editor completion and validation, and the full example shows how optional fields are organized.
guide.step2Description: These fields define the theme's identity in the community and in power-tv. Name and description can be strings or localized objects with keys such as en and zh-CN.
guide.idDescription: 3–64 letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens. Consecutive dots and the builtin. prefix are not allowed.
guide.nameDescription: Required. Up to 64 characters per language.
guide.descriptionFieldDescription: Optional. Up to 512 characters per language.
guide.versionDescription: Use major.minor.patch, such as 1.0.0. Each version of the same ID can be published only once.
guide.minAppVersionDescription: Optional. Declares the minimum power-tv version required by the theme.
guide.step3Description: schemes.light is required; schemes.dark is optional. primary and surface are enough to establish the base style; add other Material 3 roles as needed, and power-tv derives any roles you omit.
guide.contrastTip: Set foreground roles such as onPrimary and onSurface explicitly, and check text-to-background contrast. Colors support #RGB, #RRGGBB, and #AARRGGBB.
guide.extraFieldsDescription: You can also configure dataViz accent colors, system fonts, card corner radius, and dashboard layout. If you use Material Theme Builder, simply copy the exported color roles into schemes.
guide.step4Description: Place theme.json at the archive root. preview.webp is used for the community preview; backdrop images must live in the assets directory and be referenced by path in backdrop.image.
guide.checklistImages: Use PNG, JPEG, or WebP images, and make sure the extension matches the real format.
guide.checklistBackdrop: Backdrop path example: assets/backdrop.webp; dim accepts 0–0.8.
guide.checklistLicense: Make sure you have permission to use and redistribute images, fonts, and other assets.
guide.step5Description: Package from the working directory that contains theme.json. The command below includes the optional preview image and assets directory; remove those entries if you do not have them, or use a .json file directly.
guide.packagingNote: Do not package the outer directory first, or theme.json will be nested and cannot be read. Before uploading, extract the archive to inspect its structure and preview it in power-tv.
guide.step6Title: Publish to the community and import into power-tv
guide.step6Description: Sign in to the community with GitHub and upload the package. It becomes public after server validation. Later updates must keep the same theme ID and use a new, unpublished version number. Published versions cannot be overwritten, and older versions remain downloadable.
guide.importHelp: In power-tv, open Settings → Theme packages → Import, choose the downloaded .ptheme, .zip, or .json file, preview it, and apply.
guide.limitsDescription: Both the community and power-tv inspect untrusted theme packages. Files that exceed limits or have unsafe structures are rejected.
guide.securityNote: Theme packages cannot contain scripts, executables, absolute paths, or .. path segments. ZIP encryption, multi-disk archives, and ZIP64 are not supported; duplicate entries, corrupt images, and spoofed extensions are also rejected.
guide.moreDescription: The upstream official documentation maintains the latest fields, layout presets, import behavior, and known limits.

upload.loginTitle: Sign in to publish a theme
upload.loginDescription: Sign in with your GitHub account to upload a theme. The community does not ask you to create another account.
upload.notFoundDescription: The theme may not exist, or may have been deleted or hidden. Return to the catalog and choose again.
upload.notOwnerTitle: Only the original creator can update
upload.notOwnerDescription: A theme ID belongs to its original creator. You can publish your own themes, but you cannot replace another creator's work.
upload.titleNew: Bring your style into more living rooms
upload.descriptionUpdate: Upload a new package with the same theme ID. Historical versions are kept.
upload.descriptionNew: Upload a package that follows the power-tv specification. It appears in the community catalog as soon as validation passes.
upload.step1Description: Set a unique theme ID, name, version, and light scheme. The community records your GitHub identity, so you do not need to enter a username or password.
upload.step2Description: Place theme.json at the ZIP root. You can add a preview.png preview and backdrop images in the assets directory.
upload.step3Description: Only the original creator can update a theme ID. Each version number can be published once, and published files cannot be overwritten.
upload.docsDescription: View the full schema and examples
